en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Nibbāna: 2.
“Salt, Great King, is cognizable by the eye.
“Yes, venerable sir, it is cognizable by the eye.”
“You know well indeed, Great King,” [the Venerable Ānanda replied].
“But what, Bhante, is cognizable by the tongue?
“Yes, Great King, it is cognizable by the tongue.”
“But, venerable sir, does the tongue perceive all salt?
“Yes, great king, the tongue perceives all salt.
“If, venerable sir, the tongue perceives all salt, why then do they bring it by carts and oxen? Should not salt alone be brought?”
“It is not possible, Great King, to bring salt alone, for these phenomena have attained a single state yet have attained a diversity of domains: salt and heaviness.
But is it possible, Great King, to weigh salt on a scale?
“It is not possible, Great King, to weigh salt with a scale; it is heaviness that is weighed by a scale.
“You are skillful, venerable Nāgasena,” he said.
This is the second problem of Nāgasena.
